title: Building a CNN with Keras 🐍
description: Hands‑on: code a CNN for MNIST or CIFAR‑10, compile, train, and evaluate — from scratch to high accuracy.

slides.title: End‑to‑End CNN Pipeline 🛠️
slides.content:
# Plan of Attack

We’ll build a CNN for the CIFAR‑10 dataset (60,000 32×32 colour images in 10 classes). Steps:

1. Load and preprocess data.
2. Define a CNN architecture (Conv → Pool → Conv → Pool → Dense).
3. Compile (loss, optimiser, metrics).
4. Train with validation split.
5. Evaluate and plot results.

We’ll use `tensorflow.keras`.

slides.title: Load CIFAR‑10 🐍
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf

(X_train, y_train), (X_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
X_train = X_train.astype('float32') / 255.0
X_test = X_test.astype('float32') / 255.0

# Convert labels to one‑hot (or use sparse categorical crossentropy)
y_train = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y_train, 10)
y_test = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y_test, 10)

slides.title: Model Definition 🏗️
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.models import Sequential
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Conv2D, MaxPooling2D, Flatten, Dense, Dropout

model = Sequential([
    Conv2D(32, (3,3), activation='relu', padding='same', input_shape=(32,32,3)),
    MaxPooling2D((2,2)),
    Conv2D(64, (3,3), activation='relu', padding='same'),
    MaxPooling2D((2,2)),
    Flatten(),
    Dense(128, activation='relu'),
    Dropout(0.5),
    Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])
model.summary()

slides.title: Compile & Train 🏋️
slides.content:
# Set Optimizer, Loss, Metrics

```python
model.compile(optimizer='adam',
              loss='categorical_crossentropy',
              metrics=['accuracy'])

history = model.fit(X_train, y_train,
                    validation_split=0.2,
                    epochs=15,
                    batch_size=64)
```
We monitor validation accuracy to see if model is improving.

quizData.question: Why do we use categorical_crossentropy loss with softmax output?

options.text: It's the default for all Keras models
It measures the distance between predicted probability distribution and true distribution, suitable for multi‑class
It only works with binary classification

quizData.explanation: Cross‑entropy compares two probability distributions; combined with softmax, it's the standard multi‑class loss.

slides.title: Evaluate & Plot 📊
slides.codeSnippet:
test_loss, test_acc = model.evaluate(X_test, y_test, verbose=0)
print(f'Test accuracy: {test_acc:.3f}')

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.plot(history.history['accuracy'], label='train')
plt.plot(history.history['val_accuracy'], label='val')
plt.legend(); plt.show()

slides.title: Next Steps 🚀
slides.content:
## Improve This Model
- Add data augmentation (`RandomFlip`, `RandomRotation`).
- Use BatchNormalization after Conv layers.
- Increase filters or depth.
- Use a pre‑trained model (transfer learning).

This basic CNN already reaches ~70% on CIFAR‑10; with these tweaks you can exceed 85%+.
